title: Observability acceptance criteria + metric guardrails (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for defining minimum acceptance criteria and operational guardrails for observability signals across the inference stack. Goal: make it obvious when a service is 'observable enough' to ship, and provide a lightweight checklist so teams can self-certify before release.

Design principles (short):
- Instrumentation should answer questions not just emit metrics. Ask: what hypothesis would this metric help validate?
- Keep cardinality low by default; add high-card signals only behind explicit need and cost evaluation.
- Traces should reconstruct a request journey end-to-end with stable span names and a small set of key attributes.
- Dashboards are for rapid incident triage; create a compact 'investigation first' view and a separate long-tail analytics view.
- Every metric or trace signal needs an owner and an SLI mapping.

Quick checklist (ship gating):
- [ ] Health metric: a single 1m gauge that represents service availability (0|1). Owner assigned.
- [ ] Latency p50/p95/p99 for user-facing RPCs with units and buckets documented.
- [ ] Error rate (4xx/5xx split) with clear source attribution (client vs. backend).
- [ ] Traffic/throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec (inference-specific).
- [ ] Resource saturation: GPU utilization, GPU memory pressure, host CPU and network egress.
- [ ] Trace anchors: span for request enter, routing decision, model inference, cache hit/miss, response serialize.
- [ ] Dashboard: one condensed triage panel that surfaces the above 6 metrics.
- [ ] Linked runbook + owner contact in dashboard header.
- [ ] Cost estimate: proxied cost / 24h using existing cost telemetry pipeline.

Metric definitions (examples and guardrails):
- request.count (counter): increments at HTTP accept; labels: service, route, region, customer_tier. Guardrail: route cardinality <= 50 by default.
- tokens.generated (counter): increments per emitted token; labels: model_variant. Guardrail: bucket model_variant with 'open' label for unknowns.
- inference.latency.ms (histogram): capture end-to-end server time from accept to last-token-send. Buckets defined: [5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000]. Use histogram_quantile for p95/p99.
- kv_cache.hit_rate (gauge OR counter pair): prefer counters (hit.count, miss.count) to avoid gauge drift; compute rate in dashboard.
- gpu.utilization.percent (gauge): per-GPU, include cluster_pool label. Guardrail: aggregate to pool-level for dashboards to limit series explosion.

Span naming convention (tracing):
- Use short stable names, lower-hyphen separated. Examples: request.receive, routing.select-backend, model.decode, kv-cache.lookup, response.send.
- Do not include identifiers in span names. Put request id and customer id in attributes, not the name.
- Attribute set (minimum): request.id, trace.origin (hosted|dedicated|private), customer.id (hashed), model.name, model.variant, seq_len, cache_hit (bool), grpc_status/http_status.
- Max attribute cardinality guidance: do not include free-form user text or prompt contents. If needed for debug, put in sampled debug captures only.

Trace sampling and debug captures:
- Default sampling: 1% adaptive tail-sampling for production traffic across all routes.
- Increase to 5% for new/experimental routes during first 72h after rollout to capture regressions. This is enforced through rollout policy tagging (see linked confluence).
- Separate "debug capture" API that allows a user-level debug trace (with prompt) stored encrypted for 7 days, gated by ACL.

Dashboard notes (investigation-first view):
- Top row: traffic, errors (4xx/5xx stacked), p95 latency, GPU pool saturation.
- Middle row: cache hit rate, model-level p95 latency, backend call latencies (DB, LLM service), cost rate.
- Bottom row: recent traces (sampled), top error messages, active rollouts with version tags and traffic split.
- Widgets: timestamped SLO burn-down, anomaly indicator (spike detector), link to most recent canary run.
- Design point: each widget should have a one-line guidance in the tooltip: "what to look for" and "first action".

SLO/SLI mapping guidance (examples):
- SLI: inference.success_rate = 1 - (5xx_count / total_requests) measured over 5m.
- SLO: 99.9% success_rate monthly for hosted-tier endpoints; dedicated tiers negotiate separately.
- SLI: inference.p95_latency_ms measured over 5m. SLO: p95 < 200ms for low-latency routes.
- Alerting: create alerts on SLO burn rate (30m) > 2x baseline and p95 latency > threshold for 10m.

Ownership + lifecycle:
- Every metric created must declare owner, description (one-liner), and consumer list (dashboard or alert). Use tag:obs-owner:<name>.
- Quarterly metric audit: owner must confirm metric is still used or deprecate. Deprecation window: 90 days.
- New metric flow: PR with schema, unit, allowed labels, expected cardinality, and cost estimate. Small metrics can be merged with self-approval; high-card or expensive signals require obs-team review (JIRA-OBS-142).

Cost/ingest guardrails:
- Default retention for high-card metrics: 14 days; aggregated rollups for 90 days. Longer retention requires business justification.
- Sampling preferred to adding high-card labels for debug traces.
- If a proposed metric predicts >1000 new series/day, tag for capacity review and approximate monthly ingestion cost in PR.

Runbook snippets (to paste in dashboards):
- If p95 latency spikes but GPU utilization is normal: check routing.select-backend spans to find backend tail latencies. Check kv_cache.* metrics for increased miss rate.
- If GPU utilization high and latency high: consider autoscale policy, inspect queue length metrics and batch sizes.
- If error rate rises and is all 502/503: check upstream model health, recent rollouts, and backend infra. Pull a representative trace tied to failed request.id.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Convergence on exact token-metering metric (tokens.generated vs tokens billed) — finance wants a mirror of billed tokens for cost reconciliation. Owner: Priya.
- Sampling budget enforcement mechanism needs infra automation (auto throttle if sampling rate causes trace backend OOM). Action: SRE spike story.
- Backfill guidance for historical dashboards when new metrics are added — acceptable to show partial history if >7d exists.
- Decide canonical label for model variants across runtimes (model.variant vs model_revision).

Appendix: small checklist for new teams onboarding observability:
1) Read this doc + confluence OBS-standards page.
2) Create minimal metrics (health, latency, errors, traffic).
3) Open PR with metric schemas and add obs-owner tag.
4) Build a 1-panel triage dashboard and link runbook.
5) Run a 72h smoke with increased sampling. Verify traces reconstruct request.
6) Request quick review from obs-team (use JIRA-OBS-142).

Notes to self: keep this doc short; split into prescriptive quickstart + detailed policy pages. Prioritize a small set of example dashboards for inference-common routes (model-serve, cache-proxy, router).

End of draft.
